seo.title: Chapter 71 U.S. Gold & Jewelry Exports: Who Buys & Tariffs
seo.shortDescription: How much gold, silver, diamonds and jewelry the U.S. exports, who buys it, and what each top buyer charges, from 2020–2025 UN Comtrade data.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$147.97 billion** of Chapter 71 goods in 2025, up **102.5%** from 2024. Almost all of the jump is bullion: **gold (heading 7108) rose 172% to $80.6 billion, 54.5% of the chapter**, and "other precious-metal articles" (7115) rose from $1.2 billion to **$21.5 billion**. Silver (7106) is 5.5%, jewelry (7113) 8.2% and diamonds (7102) 5.3%. **Switzerland (39.4%) and the United Kingdom (21.3%) buy 61%**, and each took far more than a year earlier (+364% and +145%).

Tariffs barely matter in this chapter. Gold, silver and platinum bullion and diamonds are duty-free in Switzerland, the UK, Hong Kong, the EU, Canada, Singapore and Australia. The tariffs that exist fall on jewelry (about 2.5% in the EU, about 5% in the UAE) and on gold in India (about 6%, with one report of 15% from May 2026). China's extra 10% on all U.S. goods applies, but China bought only 0.7% of the chapter. The rules that matter are compliance rules: Kimberley Process certificates for rough diamonds, anti-money-laundering programs for dealers, and the ban on exporting luxury goods to Russia and Belarus.

keyTakeaways: Bullion drives the chapter: gold (7108) is 54.5%, other precious-metal articles (7115) 14.5% and silver (7106) 5.5%. Jewelry (7113) is 8.2% and diamonds (7102) 5.3%.
Switzerland (39.4%) and the UK (21.3%) buy 61% of the chapter, and both bought far more in 2025 (+364% and +145%). Hong Kong takes 8.5%.
Tariffs hardly matter for the largest buyers: bullion and diamonds are duty-free in Switzerland, the UK, Hong Kong, the EU, Canada, Singapore and Australia. India's gold duty is the main exception.

The U.S. side is compliance, not tariffs: a Kimberley Process certificate for rough diamonds, an anti-money-laundering program for dealers, and the ban on exporting luxury goods to Russia and Belarus.
